text: Numerical foundations: conditioning, residuals, convergence and independent references Compare AMG, QR/SVD, Krylov eigenvalue methods and quadrature across fixed conditioning families. Separate residuals from forward error and matrix from integral conditioning; check independent references alongside convergence limits and diagnostic blind spots. These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved. Download and execute the supplement Run inside atlas-foundations-conditioning-2026-11-22 from the ZIP. This command executes all 4 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it. AMG: conditioning, anisotropy, residual and forward error Separate condition number from anisotropy on SPD systems of 49, 225 and 961 unknowns. Compare analytic spectra, independent sparse direct solutions and DST diagonalization, and measure how residual translates to forward error. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries A=T⊗I+εI⊗T with n=7/15/31 and ε=1/.1/.01. This is a known-solution algebraic diagnostic; continuum PDE validation remains in the earlier Poisson example. At fixed square n, κ₂ is independent of ε. Editorial clarification This diagnoses algebraic matrix conditioning and iteration error, separately from the earlier Poisson manufactured-solution PDE accuracy. Anisotropy and the 2-norm condition number need not vary together on a fixed grid. Distinguish residual, solution error and an exhausted iteration budget. Adopted numerical method Reuse the earlier MIT-licensed Atlas educational smoothed-aggregation AMG in a separate source release. Matrix-only hierarchy setup uses strength .08, Jacobi smoothing, fixed relative tolerance 10⁻¹⁰ and at most 180 V-cycles. Perturb a maximal-eigenmode RHS in the minimal-eigenmode direction and check the predicted relative amplification κ₂ with direct solves. Isotropic runs must converge; the predeclared anisotropy stress policy permits honestly reported budget exhaustion. A one-cycle control detects nonconvergence. Official reference-implementation documentation: scipy.linalg.eigh.html · scipy.linalg.eig.html Quadrature: narrow peaks, cancellation, endpoints and estimator blind spots Vary Gauss order and adaptive tolerance on narrow Lorentz peaks, a square-root endpoint, severe cancellation, a zero integral and a deliberately missed compact bump, using analytic integrals and QUADPACK. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Use[0,1], Gauss orders8/16/32/64/128 and tolerances10⁻⁵/10⁻⁷/10⁻⁹. Editorial clarification An adaptive estimate or agreement between calculations is not a rigorous error bound for arbitrary integrands. Distinguish absolute and relative error under cancellation, unresolved local structure and evaluation budgets. Adopted numerical method Implement Golub–Welsch nodes/weights and adaptive Simpson with a local difference/15 estimate.
